resources.string: Never lose your place to look up a word
Hold your phone over the page and rest the lens on a word. Its meaning appears in under a second — no typing, no searching, and your book stays in your hands.
WordLens needs the camera to see your page. You can allow it in Settings → Permissions → Camera.
Works offline too. The camera picture never leaves your phone.
Rest the lens on a word

You\'re offline — showing the built-in dictionary

Point your phone at any book and rest the lens on a word to see what it means.

Meanings come from WordNet 3.0 (Princeton University), Simple English Wiktionary and Wiktionary (CC BY-SA), with similar and opposite words from Datamuse.

Privacy: the camera picture never leaves your phone. With update alerts on, WordLens asks GitHub now and then whether a newer version is out (an ordinary web request, like opening a page). Both can be switched off in the ⋮ menu. With simple online meanings on, the words you aim the lens at are sent (as plain text) to fetch their meanings.
